scene.bubble: Welcome to QUICK ANSWERS, the game show where long answers lose points! Yes or no, team!
scene.intro: Welcome to QUICK ANSWERS, the game show where long answers lose points! Do you like maths? Yes, I do. Has she got a bike? No, she hasn't. Were they at the concert? Yes, they were. Diego answers correctly but adds three sentences of explanation every time, so Ingrid wins easily. Short and correct — that's the rule. Ready? Answer quickly and get the point!

activities.title: Grammar · …isn't it?
activities.instructions: Read the sentences. Then choose the right ending.

data.title: That's the answer, isn't it?
data.intro: You are almost sure, and you want the other person to agree. Add a mini-question at the end — English does this all the time.
data.can: I can add a tag question (isn’t it? don’t you? did she?) to check something I think is true.

examples.text: She won the last round, didn’t she?
It isn't the correct answer, is it?

rules: Positive sentence → negative tag. Negative sentence → positive tag.
Use the same helper verb: is → isn’t · can → can’t · has → hasn’t · was → wasn’t.
No helper verb in the sentence? Then use do / does / did: "You play tennis, don’t you?"
